open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M02 — SourcePhotoObservation
open_points.text: `size` is the number of bytes read when the file was read to its end, the bytes `source_id` is the hash of; otherwise it is the size its metadata gave when it was listed. `source_id` is present for `ready`, `placed` and `published` and absent for `rejected`
open_points.question: When a file is read to its end but the resulting observation is `rejected`, is `source_id` the hash of the bytes read or is it absent?
options: Populate `source_id` whenever the file was read to its end, including for `rejected`.
Keep `source_id` absent for every `rejected` observation and treat the hash clause as applying only to non-rejected observations.
open_points.default_guess: Keep `source_id` absent for every `rejected` observation and rewrite the hash clause to make that qualification explicit.

witness.initial: A listed file has metadata size N, can be read successfully to its end, and its content is unsupported.
events: The deliverer scans the folder and reads all N bytes.
After reading the complete content, the deliverer classifies the file as `rejected` with reason `unsupported_format`.
The calling flow reads the resulting SourcePhotoObservation.
outcomes: The observation contains the hash of the N bytes as `source_id`, because those are described as the bytes `source_id` is the hash of.
The observation has `source_id = None`, because `source_id` is required to be absent for `rejected`.
